typedef struct srtp_cipher_test_case_t {
    size_t key_length_octets;        /* octets in key            */
    const uint8_t *key;              /* key                      */
    uint8_t *idx;                    /* packet index             */
    size_t plaintext_length_octets;  /* octets in plaintext      */
    const uint8_t *plaintext;        /* plaintext                */
    size_t ciphertext_length_octets; /* octets in plaintext      */
    const uint8_t *ciphertext;       /* ciphertext               */
    size_t aad_length_octets;        /* octets in AAD            */
    const uint8_t *aad;              /* AAD                      */
    size_t tag_length_octets;        /* Length of AEAD tag       */
    const struct srtp_cipher_test_case_t
        *next_test_case; /* pointer to next testcase */
} srtp_cipher_test_case_t;
objects.description: Structure describing a single cipher test vector, including key, packet index, plaintext, ciphertext, AAD, tag length, and link to the next case for chaining.
Metadata and virtual-function table for a cipher algorithm implementation: constructor/destructor, init, AAD, encrypt/decrypt, IV setter, description, test vectors, and an algorithm identifier.
Concrete cipher instance bound to a cipher type and holding implementation-specific state, key length, and algorithm id.

Vtable/descriptor for an authentication algorithm. Holds function pointers for allocation, init, incremental update/start, final compute, and deallocation, plus a description string, built-in test vectors, and an algorithm identifier. Instances are typically static singletons describing a concrete auth implementation.

Runtime authentication context instance. References an auth type (algorithm vtable), owns an opaque state pointer managed by the type, and records output tag length, key length, and any keystream prefix length. Use via the srtp_auth_* macros to init, start/update/compute, and dealloc through its type functions.
Linked-list node containing known-answer test vectors for an auth algorithm: key, message, expected tag, with lengths. Used by self-test and external test routines to validate implementations.
Function pointer type for an allocator that creates an srtp_auth_t instance and its state given key and output lengths.
Function pointer type for initializing an auth state with a key.

objects.definition: typedef struct srtp_ctx_t_ srtp_ctx_t;
objects.description: Opaque SRTP session context type. Forward-declared; definition is internal to the library. Use via the alias srtp_t.
Bitmask-like enum describing which security services are applied: confidentiality, authentication, both, or none.
Crypto policy describing algorithms and key/tag lengths for SRTP/SRTCP streams. Populated via helper functions to standard profiles.
Specifies whether an SSRC selection is a specific value or a wildcard for inbound or outbound streams.

Represents a master key along with its MKI identifier for MKI-based keying. Key storage/ownership is by the application; lengths are configured in policy.

Defines the configuration for an SRTP stream, including SSRC selector, RTP/RTCP crypto policies, master keying (single key or MKI array), replay window, retransmission allowance, optional encrypted header ids, and list linkage for multi-stream sessions.

Enumeration of standard SRTP profiles (algorithm suites). Used to populate crypto policies and query key/salt lengths.
Event codes emitted by the library for notable conditions like SSRC collision or key usage limits.
Payload passed to the user-installed event handler describing the session, SSRC, and event type.

objects.definition: typedef void(srtp_event_handler_func_t)(srtp_event_data_t *data);

Log severity levels used by the logging callback.

functions.name: srtp_cipher_get_key_length
functions.description: Returns the key length (in octets) for the given cipher instance. Use to determine the required key size for initialization or verification.
requirements: c must be a valid, non-null pointer to an srtp_cipher_t instance.
The cipher instance should have been allocated (and typically configured) so its key length is known.

functions.name: srtp_cipher_type_self_test
functions.description: Runs built-in self-tests for the specified cipher type using its embedded test vectors (key/IV/plaintext/ciphertext/AAD). Intended to validate a cipher implementation at startup or registration time.
requirements: ct must be a valid, non-null pointer to an srtp_cipher_type_t.
ct->test_data should point to a valid linked list of srtp_cipher_test_case_t entries; if absent, self-test may fail or be a no-op, depending on implementation.
The cipher type must provide working alloc/init/set_iv/encrypt/decrypt (and set_aad for AEAD) callbacks to pass the tests.
Returns an srtp_err_status_t indicating success or failure of self-test.

functions.name: srtp_cipher_type_test
functions.description: Tests a cipher type against externally supplied test vectors. Useful for validating an implementation with custom or additional vectors.
requirements: ct must be a valid, non-null pointer to an srtp_cipher_type_t with functional callbacks.

test_data must be a non-null pointer to one or more srtp_cipher_test_case_t entries linked via next_test_case and correctly populated (lengths match buffers; key/idx/aad/tag sizes appropriate for the cipher).
Caller should expect an srtp_err_status_t indicating pass/fail.

functions.name: srtp_cipher_bits_per_second
functions.signature: uint64_t srtp_cipher_bits_per_second(srtp_cipher_t *c, size_t octets_in_buffer, size_t num_trials);
functions.description: Estimates the encryption throughput of an initialized cipher instance by encrypting buffers of a given size for a number of trials and returning bits per second. Returns 0 on error.
requirements: c MUST be allocated and initialized prior to this call (as stated in the header comment).
octets_in_buffer should be greater than 0 to produce a meaningful measurement.
num_trials should be greater than 0; very small values may reduce accuracy.
Returns 0 if an error is encountered.

functions.name: srtp_cipher_type_alloc
functions.signature: srtp_err_status_t srtp_cipher_type_alloc(const srtp_cipher_type_t *ct, srtp_cipher_t **c, size_t key_len, size_t tlen);
functions.description: Allocates (but does not initialize) a cipher instance of the given type, with the specified key length and tag length (for AEAD ciphers). Use srtp_cipher_init to set the key after allocation.
requirements: ct must be a valid, non-null cipher type whose alloc function supports the requested key_len and tag length.
c must be a non-null pointer to receive the allocated srtp_cipher_t*.
key_len must be a supported key size for the cipher type.
tlen (tag length) must be supported by the cipher type; for non-AEAD ciphers, this may need to be zero depending on implementation.
Caller is responsible for calling srtp_cipher_dealloc on success to avoid leaks.
After successful allocation, srtp_cipher_init must be called before encryption/decryption.

functions.name: srtp_cipher_dealloc
functions.description: Deallocates a cipher instance previously created via srtp_cipher_type_alloc.
requirements: c must be a cipher previously returned by srtp_cipher_type_alloc (or equivalent).
c should be non-null.
After deallocation, c must not be used.

functions.name: srtp_cipher_init
functions.description: Initializes or re-initializes a cipher instance with the provided key material.
requirements: c must have been successfully allocated by srtp_cipher_type_alloc.
key must be non-null and contain exactly the number of octets reported by srtp_cipher_get_key_length(c).
Must be called before set_iv/output/encrypt/decrypt.
Re-initialization overwrites previous keying material.

functions.name: srtp_cipher_set_iv
functions.description: Sets the initialization vector (IV) for the cipher for either encryption or decryption, depending on direction. Typically required per-packet for SRTP/SRTCP.
requirements: c must be allocated and initialized with a key.
iv must be non-null and sized appropriately for the cipher/transform.
direction must be one of srtp_direction_encrypt, srtp_direction_decrypt, or srtp_direction_any; choose appropriately for the intended operation.
Must be called before encrypt/decrypt when the cipher requires an IV.

functions.name: srtp_cipher_output
functions.description: Generates cipher output bytes (e.g., keystream for stream ciphers) into buffer. The number of requested bytes is provided via *num_octets_to_output on input; the function may update it with the number actually written.
requirements: c must be allocated and initialized; IV must be set if required by the cipher.
buffer must be non-null and large enough to hold at least *num_octets_to_output bytes on input.
num_octets_to_output must be non-null; on input it specifies the requested number of octets; on output it may be updated to the number produced.
For AEAD or block modes that don’t support raw output, this may fail depending on cipher type.

functions.name: srtp_cipher_encrypt
functions.signature: srtp_err_status_t srtp_cipher_encrypt(srtp_cipher_t *c, const uint8_t *src, size_t src_len, uint8_t *dst, size_t *dst_len);
functions.description: Encrypts src_len bytes from src into dst. For stream or some block modes, src and dst may refer to the same buffer for in-place operation. For AEAD ciphers, any AAD must be set first and the authentication tag length is determined by the cipher configuration.
requirements: c must be allocated and initialized; IV must be set if required by the cipher.
src must be non-null if src_len > 0.
dst must be non-null with capacity of at least *dst_len bytes on input; on return, *dst_len is set to the number of bytes written.
dst_len must be non-null; on input it provides the available output capacity.
If performing in-place encryption, dst may equal src; otherwise, buffers must not overlap improperly.
For AEAD ciphers, srtp_cipher_set_aad must be called (as needed) before encrypt.

functions.name: srtp_cipher_decrypt
functions.signature: srtp_err_status_t srtp_cipher_decrypt(srtp_cipher_t *c, const uint8_t *src, size_t src_len, uint8_t *dst, size_t *dst_len);
functions.description: Decrypts src_len bytes from src into dst. For some ciphers, decryption can be in-place (dst == src). For AEAD ciphers, any AAD used during encryption must be supplied via srtp_cipher_set_aad prior to decryption to authenticate correctly.
requirements: c must be allocated and initialized; IV must be set to match the ciphertext’s IV/nonce.
src must be non-null if src_len > 0.
dst must be non-null with capacity of at least *dst_len bytes on input; on return, *dst_len is set to the number of bytes written.
dst_len must be non-null; on input it provides the available output capacity.
If performing in-place decryption, dst may equal src; otherwise, buffers must not overlap improperly.
For AEAD ciphers, the exact same AAD used during encryption must be set via srtp_cipher_set_aad before decryption or authentication will fail.

functions.name: srtp_cipher_set_aad
functions.signature: srtp_err_status_t srtp_cipher_set_aad(srtp_cipher_t *c, const uint8_t *aad, size_t aad_len);
functions.description: Supplies Additional Authenticated Data (AAD) to AEAD ciphers to be authenticated but not encrypted. Must be called before the corresponding encrypt/decrypt operation.
requirements: c must be allocated and initialized; IV must be set if required by the cipher flow.
aad may be null only if aad_len is zero; otherwise must be non-null and point to aad_len bytes.
aad_len must be the exact length of the AAD to authenticate and must be supported by the cipher.
Applicable only to AEAD cipher types; non-AEAD ciphers may return an error.

functions.name: srtp_replace_cipher_type
functions.description: Replaces the existing cipher implementation registered under the given cipher type id with a new implementation. The replacement must pass the original cipher type’s self-tests as well as its own.
requirements: ct must be a valid, non-null pointer to a fully implemented srtp_cipher_type_t (alloc/dealloc/init/set_iv/encrypt/decrypt and set_aad if AEAD).
id must specify the cipher type being replaced and should correspond to ct’s implementation.
The new cipher must pass both the existing implementation’s self-tests and its own (explicitly stated in the header).
Should be called before creating/using cipher instances that depend on the replaced type.

functions.name: srtp_auth_get_key_length
functions.description: Returns the length, in octets, of the key configured for the given SRTP authentication context. Use this to query how many key bytes the auth instance expects or is using.
requirements: a must be a non-null pointer to a valid, initialized srtp_auth_t instance.
The srtp_auth_t instance must have been allocated/initialized such that its key length field is set; otherwise the returned value may be undefined by the implementation.

functions.name: srtp_auth_get_tag_length
functions.description: Returns the length, in octets, of the authentication tag produced by the given SRTP authentication context. Use this to size output buffers for MAC/tag generation and verification.
requirements: a must be a non-null pointer to a valid, initialized srtp_auth_t instance.
The srtp_auth_t instance must have a defined output tag length; otherwise the returned value may be undefined by the implementation.

functions.name: srtp_auth_get_prefix_length
functions.description: Returns the length, in octets, of any keystream prefix used by the given SRTP authentication context. This is typically zero for most MACs; non-zero values indicate the authenticator uses a prefix.
requirements: a must be a non-null pointer to a valid, initialized srtp_auth_t instance.
The srtp_auth_t instance must have a defined prefix length; otherwise the returned value may be undefined by the implementation.

functions.name: srtp_auth_type_self_test
functions.description: Runs built-in self-tests for the given authentication algorithm type using the test vectors embedded in the type (at->test_data). Intended to verify correctness of an auth implementation before use.
requirements: at must be a non-null pointer to a valid srtp_auth_type_t.
at->test_data should reference a list/array of known-good test cases (key/data/tag triples); if none are provided, behavior is implementation-defined.
Returns an srtp_err_status_t status code; specific values depend on the implementation (typically success on all vectors matching, error otherwise).

functions.name: srtp_auth_type_test
functions.description: Tests the specified authentication algorithm type against externally supplied test cases. Useful for validating an auth implementation with custom or additional vectors.
requirements: at must be a non-null pointer to a valid srtp_auth_type_t.
test_data must be a non-null pointer to one or more srtp_auth_test_case_t entries, typically linked via the next_test_case pointer.
Each test case must provide consistent lengths and non-null buffers for key (key_length_octets and key), data (data_length_octets and data), and tag (tag_length_octets and tag).
Returns an srtp_err_status_t status code; specific values depend on the implementation (typically success on all vectors matching, error otherwise).

functions.name: srtp_replace_auth_type
functions.description: Replaces the SRTP library’s registered implementation for the given auth type identifier with a new implementation. The new implementation must pass both the existing implementation’s self-tests and its own self-tests before replacement is accepted.
requirements: ct must be a non-null pointer to a fully defined srtp_auth_type_t implementation (alloc, dealloc, init, compute, update, start, and associated fields as required by the implementation).
id must be a valid srtp_auth_type_id_t corresponding to the algorithm being replaced.
The new implementation must pass all relevant self-tests (both the current registered type’s and its own), as stated in the header comments; if tests fail, the replacement must not occur.
Caller must check the returned srtp_err_status_t to determine success or failure.

functions.name: srtp_init
functions.description: Initializes the libSRTP library. Must be called before any other SRTP API function. Typical usage is once at process start prior to creating sessions/streams.
requirements: Must be called before any other SRTP functions.
Return value must be checked for srtp_err_status_ok; otherwise the library is not initialized.
Thread-safety/one-time initialization behavior is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: srtp_shutdown
functions.description: De-initializes the libSRTP library. After this call no SRTP API functions may be used.
requirements: Must not call any SRTP functions after successful shutdown.
Return value should be checked; on success, the library is de-initialized.
Order: intended to be called after srtp_init().

functions.name: srtp_protect
functions.signature: srtp_err_status_t srtp_protect(srtp_t ctx, const uint8_t *rtp, size_t rtp_len, uint8_t *srtp, size_t *srtp_len, size_t mki_index);
functions.description: Applies SRTP protection to an outbound RTP packet using the given session context. Supports in-place operation (srtp buffer may alias rtp).
requirements: ctx must be a valid SRTP session created with srtp_create().
rtp must point to a complete RTP packet, 32-bit aligned (alignment requirement stated).
rtp_len must be the length in octets of the complete RTP packet.
srtp must point to a buffer large enough to hold the protected packet (may be the same pointer as rtp for in-place).
*srtp_len must contain the size of the srtp buffer on input and will be updated with the protected packet size on success; on error its value is undefined.
RTP sequence numbers presented need not be consecutive but must be out-of-order by less than 2^15 (32768).
If MKI is used (policy.use_mki true), mki_index selects the key; otherwise it is ignored.
Caller must handle srtp_err_status_buffer_small if the output buffer is too small.
Return value must be checked for srtp_err_status_ok before using output.

functions.name: srtp_unprotect
functions.signature: srtp_err_status_t srtp_unprotect(srtp_t ctx, const uint8_t *srtp, size_t srtp_len, uint8_t *rtp, size_t *rtp_len);
functions.description: Verifies and removes SRTP protection from an inbound SRTP packet using the given session context. Supports in-place operation (rtp buffer may alias srtp).
requirements: ctx must be a valid SRTP session created with srtp_create().
srtp must point to a complete SRTP packet, 32-bit aligned (alignment requirement stated).
srtp_len must be the length of the complete SRTP packet.
rtp must point to a buffer large enough to hold the resulting RTP packet (may be the same pointer as srtp for in-place).
*rtp_len must contain the size of the rtp buffer on input and will be updated with the RTP packet size on success; on error its value is undefined.
RTP sequence numbers received need not be consecutive but must be out-of-order by less than 2^15 (32768).
Caller must handle authentication failure (srtp_err_status_auth_fail), replay failure (srtp_err_status_replay_fail), and bad MKI (srtp_err_status_bad_mki).
Return value must be checked for srtp_err_status_ok before using output.

functions.name: srtp_create
functions.description: Allocates and initializes an SRTP session context, optionally applying a policy (or linked list of policies) describing streams to add immediately.
requirements: session must be a valid pointer to receive the created session handle.
policy may be NULL or point to a srtp_policy_t (or list).
If a list is provided, the final element must have next == NULL.
Any wildcard SSRC use must follow documented constraints in srtp_policy_t (cannot match both inbound and outbound).
Caller must check return value for allocation or initialization failures before using the session.

functions.name: srtp_stream_add
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new SRTP stream within an existing SRTP session using the provided policy.
requirements: session must be a valid SRTP session created by srtp_create().
policy must point to a valid srtp_policy_t for the stream to add (single element).
Caller must check return value for allocation/initialization errors.

functions.name: srtp_stream_remove
functions.description: Removes and deallocates a specific SRTP stream from a session by SSRC.
requirements: session must be a valid SRTP session.
ssrc is in host byte order (changed in 3.0.0).
Wildcard SSRC values cannot be removed.
Caller must check return value to determine success.

functions.name: srtp_update
functions.description: Updates all streams in a session according to the supplied policy (or list), preserving each stream’s ROC (roll-over counter).
requirements: session must be a valid SRTP session.
policy must point to a srtp_policy_t or list; final element must have next == NULL.
Caller must check return value for allocation/initialization errors or other failures.
Semantics of how streams are matched/updated beyond preserving ROC are not detailed here (unknown).

functions.name: srtp_stream_update
functions.description: Updates stream(s) in the session that match the provided policy, preserving ROC for those streams.
requirements: session must be a valid SRTP session.
policy must describe the target stream(s) to update.
Caller must check return value for allocation/initialization errors or other failures.
Exact matching rules between policy and streams are not detailed here (unknown).

functions.name: srtp_crypto_policy_set_rtp_default
functions.description: Initializes a crypto policy structure to the SRTP default policy for RTP protection. Convenience setter to avoid manual field-by-field initialization.
requirements: p must be a valid, writable pointer to a srtp_crypto_policy_t.

functions.name: srtp_crypto_policy_set_rtcp_default
functions.description: Initializes a crypto policy structure to the SRTP default policy for RTCP protection.
requirements: p must be a valid, writable pointer to a srtp_crypto_policy_t.

functions.name: srtp_crypto_policy_set_aes_cm_128_hmac_sha1_32
functions.description: Sets a crypto policy to AES-128 Counter Mode with HMAC-SHA1 and a 32-bit auth tag (RFC 4568). Intended for SRTP with short tags; not recommended for SRTCP.
requirements: p must be a valid, writable pointer to a srtp_crypto_policy_t.

functions.name: srtp_crypto_policy_set_aes_cm_128_null_auth
functions.description: Sets a crypto policy to AES-128 Counter Mode encryption with no authentication. Not recommended except when unavoidable (especially not for SRTCP).
requirements: p must be a valid, writable pointer to a srtp_crypto_policy_t.

functions.name: srtp_crypto_policy_set_null_cipher_hmac_sha1_80
functions.description: Sets a crypto policy to HMAC-SHA1 with 80-bit tag for authentication only (no encryption). Not recommended unless encryption must be forgone.
requirements: p must be a valid, writable pointer to a srtp_crypto_policy_t.

functions.name: srtp_crypto_policy_set_null_cipher_hmac_null
functions.description: Sets a crypto policy to no encryption and no authentication. Intended only for testing and troubleshooting.

# Target stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR to build keys and fill test vectors. Our goal is to
# emit a bytes buffer that, when sliced/loop-appended by the fuzz stubs, yields
# valid-length binary material for keys, IV-like indexes, plaintext/ciphertext, AAD, and tags.
# Strategy:
# - Construct a compact container with multiple concatenated sections of high-entropy bytes,
#   covering common SRTP/SRTCP cipher/auth key sizes and AEAD needs.
# - Include several canonical key sizes: 16, 24, 32 (AES-128/192/256), plus salts (14 bytes),

# - Provide variable-length payload segments to satisfy arbitrary requested lengths by repetition.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Seeded randomness for reproducibility via seed argument.

# Helper to generate deterministic pseudo-random bytes with some structured subpatterns

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix of random bytes and subtle patterns (incrementing counters, repeating blocks)
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < n:
        mode = rng.randint(0, 4)
        remaining = n - len(out)
        if mode == 0:
            # pure random chunk
            chunk = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(min(remaining, rng.randint(16, 64))))
            out.extend(chunk)
        elif mode == 1:
            # repeating 16-byte block
            blk = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(16))
            reps = max(1, min(remaining // 16, rng.randint(1, 8)))
            out.extend(blk * reps)
        elif mode == 2:
            # ascending counter from random start
            start = rng.randrange(0, 256)
            cnt = bytearray((start + i) & 0xFF for i in range(min(remaining, rng.randint(16, 128))))
            out.extend(cnt)
        elif mode == 3:
            # descending counter
            start = rng.randrange(0, 256)
            cnt = bytearray((start - i) & 0xFF for i in range(min(remaining, rng.randint(16, 128))))
            out.extend(cnt)
        else:
            # XOR two random sequences
            m = min(remaining, rng.randint(16, 64))
            a = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(m))
            b = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(m))
            out.extend(bytes(x ^ y for x, y in zip(a, b)))
    return bytes(out[:n])

import random
from typing import List

# Data type: raw binary IV/nonce
# Target stubs consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR to obtain:
#  - An IV buffer (will be resized to at least 32 bytes). Larger and
#    varied sizes are fine; contents are arbitrary bytes.
#  - Multiple buffers for srtp_cipher_test_case_t fields: key, idx (16 bytes),
#    plaintext, ciphertext, aad. The stub concatenates FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
#    as needed to reach required lengths, so returning a reasonably rich
#    byte sequence that contains diverse patterns, sizes, and alignments
#    helps produce valid, interesting test vectors without relying on
#    malformed data.
#
# Strategy:
#  - Produce a composite byte buffer containing a sequence of segments.
#  - Each segment is length-prefixed and contains different byte patterns
#    commonly useful for crypto inputs: all-zero, all-0xFF, low/high
#    entropy PRNG bytes, incrementing counters, repeating short patterns,
#    and RTP-like header bytes for realism.
#  - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
#  - Deterministic w.r.t. seed.
#
# The fuzzer harness will slice/concatenate from FUZZ_PARAM_STR data to fill
# required buffers. Providing many varied segments increases chances of
# generating consistent key/pt/ct/aad lengths while staying valid.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _u16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return x.to_bytes(2, 'big')

def _u32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return x.to_bytes(4, 'big')

def _mk_all_zero(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([0] * n)

def _mk_all_ff(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([0xFF] * n)

def _mk_inc(n: int, start: int = 0) -> bytes:
    return bytes([(start + i) & 0xFF for i in range(n)])

def _mk_pattern(n: int, pat: bytes) -> bytes:
    if not pat:
        return b""
    return (pat * (n // len(pat) + 1))[:n]

def _mk_prng(n: int, rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rnd.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _mk_rtp_like(n: int, rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal RTP header (12 bytes) + payload
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    v_p_x_cc = 0x80 | rnd.randrange(0, 16)  # V=2, CC random
    m_pt = (rnd.randrange(0, 2) << 7) | rnd.randrange(0, 128)
    seq = rnd.randrange(0, 65536)
    ts = rnd.randrange(0, 2**32)
    ssrc = rnd.randrange(0, 2**32)
    header = bytes([v_p_x_cc, m_pt]) + _u16(seq) + _u32(ts) + _u32(ssrc)
    if n <= len(header):
        return header[:n]
    payload = _mk_prng(n - len(header), rnd)
    return header + payload

def _lp(segment: bytes) -> bytes:
    # 2-byte length prefix (big endian) to help the consumer split if it wants.
    # The fuzz harness here just concatenates, but a length prefix is harmless
    # and provides diversity; it may be ignored by the consumer.
    l = len(segment)
    return _u16(l) + segment

def _build_segments(rnd: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    segs: List[bytes] = []

    # Choose a base IV size around common SRTP nonces (AES-CTR 16, GCM 12)
    iv_sizes = [12, 16, 24, 32, 48]
    rnd.shuffle(iv_sizes)

    # Include key-like sizes typical for SRTP profiles: 16, 24, 32 plus salts (14)
    key_sizes = [16, 24, 32, 30, 46]
    rnd.shuffle(key_sizes)

    # Construct a mix of segments
    for n in iv_sizes:
        segs.append(_lp(_mk_all_zero(n)))
        segs.append(_lp(_mk_all_ff(n)))
        segs.append(_lp(_mk_inc(n, rnd.randrange(0, 256))))
        segs.append(_lp(_mk_prng(n, rnd)))
        segs.append(_lp(_mk_pattern(n, b"\xAA\x55")))

    for n in key_sizes:
        # Mix of PRNG and structured patterns
        segs.append(_lp(_mk_prng(n, rnd)))
        segs.append(_lp(_mk_inc(n)))
        segs.append(_lp(_mk_pattern(n, b"\x00\x01\x02\x03")))

    # Add several RTP-like headers to serve as AAD/plaintext seeds
    for n in [12, 20, 36, 64, 128]:
        segs.append(_lp(_mk_rtp_like(n, rnd)))

    # Additional variable-length segments to satisfy arbitrary lengths the stub requests
    for _ in range(10):
        n = rnd.randrange(8, 256)
        choice = rnd.randrange(0, 6)
        if choice == 0:
            seg = _mk_prng(n, rnd)
        elif choice == 1:
            seg = _mk_inc(n, rnd.randrange(0, 256))
        elif choice == 2:
            seg = _mk_pattern(n, rnd.choice([b"\x13", b"\x00\xFF", b"\xDE\xAD\xBE\xEF"]))
        elif choice == 3:
            seg = _mk_all_zero(n)
        elif choice == 4:
            seg = _mk_all_ff(n)
        else:
            seg = _mk_rtp_like(n, rnd)
        segs.append(_lp(seg))

    # Include a couple of 16-byte segments expressly for idx buffers
    for _ in range(4):
        segs.append(_lp(_mk_prng(16, rnd)))

    return segs


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Randomize segment order slightly for more variety across seeds
    segs = _build_segments(rnd)
    rnd.shuffle(segs)

    # Concatenate until MAX_TOTAL
    out = bytearray()
    for s in segs:
        if len(out) + len(s) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out.extend(s)

    # Ensure we have at least 64 bytes total to comfortably satisfy the IV path
    # in the stub (which resizes to 32 if shorter). Add a final PRNG tail if needed.
    if len(out) < 64:
        tail_len = min(128, MAX_TOTAL - len(out))
        out.extend(_lp(_mk_prng(tail_len - 2, rnd)))

    return bytes(out)

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets arbitrary binary data inputs used by the libSRTP fuzz stubs.
# Strategy:
# - Produce buffers that are likely valid and interesting for IVs, plaintext/ciphertext, AAD, and
#   opaque user data. The fuzz stubs request varying lengths (often up to 1024) via FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# - We assemble a composite buffer containing several segments with different lengths and content
#   styles (structured, zeroes, ascending bytes, random, repeated patterns) so that repeated calls
#   to FUZZ_PARAM_STR will slice different parts while remaining plausible.
# - Limit total size to <= 4096 bytes.
# - Seeded randomness for reproducibility.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _pattern_repeat(block: bytes, total: int) -> bytes:
    if not block:
        return b""
    reps, rem = divmod(total, len(block))
    return block * reps + block[:rem]

def _make_ivs(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Common SRTP IV/nonce sizes include 12, 16, and 32 bytes; stub pads to >=32 sometimes.
    sizes = [12, 16, 32]
    ivs = []
    for s in sizes:
        # Mix fixed patterns with random material
        base = bytearray(_rand_bytes(rng, s))
        if s >= 12:
            # Put realistic SSRC/seq/ROC-like fields for variety
            # Not truly SRTP-formatted, just plausible-looking binary structure
            # [SSRC(4)][seq(2)][ts(4)][misc]
            ssrc = rng.randrange(0, 2**32)
            seq = rng.randrange(0, 2**16)
            ts  = rng.randrange(0, 2**32)
            struct.pack_into('>I', base, 0, ssrc)
            if s >= 6:
                struct.pack_into('>H', base, 4, seq)
            if s >= 10:
                struct.pack_into('>I', base, 6, ts)
        ivs.append(bytes(base))
    return ivs

def _make_keys(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Typical SRTP master key lengths: 16, 24, 32 bytes. Include salt appended (14 bytes is common).
    keys = []
    for klen in (16, 24, 32):
        key = _rand_bytes(rng, klen)
        # Optionally append salt to emulate srtp_append_salt_to_key use
        salt_len = rng.choice([0, 14])
        if salt_len:
            salt = _rand_bytes(rng, salt_len)
            key = key + salt
        keys.append(key)
    return keys

def _make_aad(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # AEAD AAD sizes vary; include empty, small, and moderate sizes
    aads = [b"", b"RTPHDR", _rand_bytes(rng, 8), _rand_bytes(rng, 16), _rand_bytes(rng, 24), _rand_bytes(rng, 32)]
    return aads

def _make_payloads(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    payloads: List[bytes] = []
    # 1) Ascending bytes 0..255 repeated
    payloads.append(_pattern_repeat(bytes(range(256)), 300))
    # 2) Zero block (useful for stream ciphers)
    payloads.append(b"\x00" * 512)
    # 3) Random small/medium
    for n in (1, 13, 64, 127, 128, 255, 512, 1024):
        payloads.append(_rand_bytes(rng, n))
    # 4) Repeated small patterns
    for patt in (b"A", b"\xFF\x00", b"SRTP", b"\x01\x02\x03\x04"):
        payloads.append(_pattern_repeat(patt, rng.randrange(16, 256)))
    return payloads

def _make_tags(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # AEAD tags common size: 16; HMAC-SHA1: 10 (80-bit) or 4 (32-bit)
    tags = [
        _rand_bytes(rng, 16),
        _rand_bytes(rng, 10),
        _rand_bytes(rng, 4)
    ]
    return tags

def _pack_len_prefixed(chunks: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Simple container: [count][len|data]* using 2-byte big-endian lengths for compactness
    out = bytearray()
    out += struct.pack('>H', len(chunks))
    for c in chunks:
        out += struct.pack('>H', len(c))
        out += c
    return bytes(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a catalog of candidate buffers
    ivs = _make_ivs(rng)
    keys = _make_keys(rng)
    aads = _make_aad(rng)
    payloads = _make_payloads(rng)
    tags = _make_tags(rng)

    # Also include a couple of composite RTP-like frames (very rough):
    def rtp_like(pt_len: int) -> bytes:
        # V=2,P=0,X=0,CC=0, M random, PT random
        vpxcc = 0x80  # V=2
        m_pt = (rng.randrange(0, 2) << 7) | rng.randrange(0, 64)
        seq = rng.randrange(0, 2**16)
        ts = rng.randrange(0, 2**32)
        ssrc = rng.randrange(0, 2**32)
        hdr = struct.pack('>BBHII', vpxcc, m_pt, seq, ts, ssrc)
        pay = _rand_bytes(rng, pt_len)
        return hdr + pay

    rtp_frames = [rtp_like(n) for n in (12, 80, 160, 400)]

    # Assemble sections with a simple header identifying groups to help stubs that reuse FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    # Sections: IVs, Keys, AADs, Payloads, Tags, RTP-like
    sections = []
    sections.append(b"IV\x00" + _pack_len_prefixed(ivs))
    sections.append(b"KY\x00" + _pack_len_prefixed(keys))
    sections.append(b"AD\x00" + _pack_len_prefixed(aads))
    sections.append(b"PL\x00" + _pack_len_prefixed(payloads))
    sections.append(b"TG\x00" + _pack_len_prefixed(tags))
    sections.append(b"RP\x00" + _pack_len_prefixed(rtp_frames))

    # Shuffle sections to vary positions per seed slightly
    rng.shuffle(sections)

    blob = b"".join(sections)

    # Ensure size constraints; trim if necessary, but keep at least 1KB to satisfy generous requests
    max_len = min(MAX_TOTAL, 4096)
    if len(blob) > max_len:
        blob = blob[:max_len]

    # Guarantee minimum size so FUZZ_PARAM_STR callers that expect up to ~1024 bytes have room
    if len(blob) < 1024:
        blob += _rand_bytes(rng, 1024 - len(blob))

    return blob

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces a valid RTP packet byte sequence suitable for the srtp_protect fuzzer stub.
# Constraints from stub:
# - Length must be a multiple of 4 (32-bit aligned).
# - Length must be >= 12 bytes (minimum RTP header size).
# - Contents should resemble valid RTP to exercise different code paths in SRTP.
# We construct RTP packets with plausible headers and variable payload sizes. We randomize key header
# fields (version=2, padding/extension/CSRC count, marker, payload type, sequence number, timestamp,
# SSRC, optional CSRC list, optional extension header) and payload content. We keep overall size <=4096.

RTP_VERSION = 2

PT_INTERESTING = [0, 8, 9, 13, 96, 97, 98, 100, 101, 111, 127]

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
MIN_RTP_HEADER = 12


def _rand_bool(r: random.Random, p_true: float = 0.5) -> bool:
    return r.random() < p_true


def _choose_payload_size(r: random.Random, base_header_len: int) -> int:
    # Ensure total length multiple of 4, and within MAX_TOTAL.
    # Prefer a variety of sizes: tiny, moderate, larger.
    target_classes = [16, 48, 120, 512, 1200, 2048, 3072]
    target = r.choice(target_classes)
    # Leave room for padding if P bit set; we'll adjust later.
    max_payload = max(0, min(MAX_TOTAL - base_header_len - 16, target))
    if max_payload <= 0:
        max_payload = 0
    # Randomize around target
    span = max(0, min(256, max_payload))
    payload = r.randint(0, span) if span > 0 else 0
    return payload


def _build_rtp(seed_r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    r = seed_r

    version = RTP_VERSION
    padding = _rand_bool(r, 0.25)
    extension = _rand_bool(r, 0.35)
    csrc_count = r.randint(0, 4)  # up to 4 CSRCs to diversify header length

    marker = _rand_bool(r, 0.3)
    payload_type = r.choice(PT_INTERESTING)

    seq = r.randrange(0, 1 << 16)
    timestamp = r.getrandbits(32)
    ssrc = r.getrandbits(32)

    # Base header without CSRCs and extension is 12 bytes
    base_header = bytearray(12)
    b0 = (version & 0x3) << 6
    b0 |= (1 if padding else 0) << 5
    b0 |= (1 if extension else 0) << 4
    b0 |= (csrc_count & 0x0F)

    b1 = (1 if marker else 0) << 7
    b1 |= (payload_type & 0x7F)

    base_header[0] = b0
    base_header[1] = b1
    struct.pack_into("!H", base_header, 2, seq)
    struct.pack_into("!I", base_header, 4, timestamp)
    struct.pack_into("!I", base_header, 8, ssrc)

    csrcs = bytearray()
    for _ in range(csrc_count):
        csrcs += struct.pack("!I", r.getrandbits(32))

    ext = bytearray()
    ext_len_words = 0
    if extension:
        # RFC 3550 extension: 16-bit profile id, 16-bit length in 32-bit words
        ext_profile = r.randrange(0, 0x10000)
        # keep small to stay within limits
        ext_len_words = r.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7])
        ext_header = struct.pack("!HH", ext_profile, ext_len_words)
        ext_payload = r.randbytes(ext_len_words * 4) if hasattr(r, 'randbytes') else bytes([r.randrange(256) for _ in range(ext_len_words * 4)])
        ext = bytearray(ext_header + ext_payload)

    header_len = len(base_header) + len(csrcs) + len(ext)

    payload_len = _choose_payload_size(r, header_len)
    payload = (r.randbytes(payload_len) if hasattr(r, 'randbytes') else bytes([r.randrange(256) for _ in range(payload_len)]))

    # Apply padding if set: last byte is pad count; pad bytes are arbitrary, but all counted.
    pad_len = 0
    if padding:
        # choose small padding to keep total size reasonable and aligned
        pad_choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12, 16]
        pad_len = r.choice(pad_choices)
        if pad_len == 0:
            padding = False
            base_header[0] &= ~(1 << 5)
        else:
            # pad bytes: last byte equals pad length, others arbitrary
            pass

    pkt = bytearray()
    pkt += base_header
    pkt += csrcs
    pkt += ext
    pkt += payload

    if pad_len:
        if pad_len == 1:
            pad_bytes = bytes([1])
        else:
            rnd = (seed_r.randbytes(pad_len - 1) if hasattr(seed_r, 'randbytes') else bytes([seed_r.randrange(256) for _ in range(pad_len - 1)]))
            pad_bytes = rnd + bytes([pad_len & 0xFF])
        pkt += pad_bytes

    # Ensure 32-bit alignment by adding zero bytes if needed (this maintains validity in stub).
    rem = len(pkt) & 3
    if rem != 0:
        pkt += b"\x00" * (4 - rem)

    # Guarantee minimum RTP header length
    if len(pkt) < MIN_RTP_HEADER:
        pkt += b"\x00" * (MIN_RTP_HEADER - len(pkt))

    # Clamp to MAX_TOTAL (should already be below), trim payload if necessary while preserving alignment
    if len(pkt) > MAX_TOTAL:
        # trim from payload area but keep multiple of 4
        trim = len(pkt) - MAX_TOTAL
        trim = (trim + 3) & ~3
        if trim < len(payload):
            pkt = pkt[:-trim]
        else:
            pkt = pkt[:MAX_TOTAL]
            # re-align
            pkt += b"\x00" * ((4 - (len(pkt) & 3)) & 3)

    return bytes(pkt)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    return _build_rtp(r)

import random
import struct
from typing import Tuple

# This generator produces plausible SRTP packets (RTP header + payload + auth tag [+ optional MKI]).
# We do NOT know the session keys or policies used by the fuzz target, so we cannot produce
# cryptographically valid tags for that unknown session. However, many fuzz harnesses accept
# structurally valid SRTP packets and will proceed through header parsing, index/MKI handling,
# and trailer sizing before ultimately returning errors only after deeper checks. To maximize
# useful coverage while remaining valid structurally, we generate:
# - Well-formed RTP headers with variable CSRC counts and optional header extension
# - Payload lengths covering small and larger sizes
# - An SRTP trailer sized consistently with common profiles
# - Word (4-byte) alignment as required by the stub
#
# We vary fields such as version, padding bit, extension bit, marker, payload type, sequence,
# timestamp, SSRC, CSRC list, and optional header extension. We then append a trailer sized to
# match common SRTP policies: auth tag of 10 bytes (80-bit), 4 bytes (32-bit), or AEAD 16 bytes,
# and optionally an MKI of random length (0-4 bytes). We also consider the SRTCP-E bit not relevant here.
#
# Note: These packets are not guaranteed to authenticate against the active session; the goal is to
# supply validly structured buffers that exercise parsing/length/alignment logic in srtp_unprotect().

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Common SRTP auth tag sizes (bytes):
COMMON_TAG_SIZES = [10, 4, 16]
# Occasional MKI sizes used in practice are small; keep within a few bytes for test harness
COMMON_MKI_SIZES = [0, 1, 2, 4]


def _rand32(r: random.Random) -> int:
    return r.getrandbits(32)


def _rand16(r: random.Random) -> int:
    return r.getrandbits(16)


def _build_rtp_header(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # RTP fixed header first 12 bytes
    version = 2  # always version 2
    padding = r.choice([0, 1])
    extension = r.choice([0, 1])
    csrc_count = r.randrange(0, 4)  # 0..3 CSRCs to keep size moderate
    marker = r.choice([0, 1])
    payload_type = r.randrange(0, 128)  # 7 bits
    seq = _rand16(r)
    timestamp = _rand32(r)
    ssrc = _rand32(r)

    b0 = (version << 6) | (padding << 5) | (extension << 4) | (csrc_count & 0x0F)
    b1 = ((marker & 0x01) << 7) | (payload_type & 0x7F)

    header = bytearray()
    header += struct.pack("!BBHII", b0, b1, seq, timestamp, ssrc)

    # Add CSRC list
    for _ in range(csrc_count):
        header += struct.pack("!I", _rand32(r))

    # Optional header extension (RFC 3550): 16-bit profile, 16-bit length in 32-bit words
    if extension:
        ext_profile = r.choice([0xBEDE, 0x1000, _rand16(r)])
        # choose total extension data length in 32-bit words, keep small
        ext_words = r.randrange(0, 5)
        header += struct.pack("!HH", ext_profile, ext_words)
        if ext_words:
            # fill with random bytes; multiple of 4 guaranteed
            header += r.randbytes(ext_words * 4)

    return bytes(header)


def _build_rtp_payload(r: random.Random, max_payload: int) -> bytes:
    # Choose a payload size that leaves room for the SRTP trailer and keeps total <= MAX_TOTAL
    # We target a variety of payload sizes, including small and larger ones
    if max_payload <= 0:
        return b""
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 32, 64, 120, 160, 320, 480, 800, 1200]
    size = r.choice([s for s in choices if s <= max_payload] or [min(12, max_payload)])
    return r.randbytes(size)


def _choose_trailer_sizes(r: random.Random) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    tag_len = r.choice(COMMON_TAG_SIZES)
    # Bias MKI to zero most of the time but include some non-zero
    mki_len = r.choices(COMMON_MKI_SIZES, weights=[6, 1, 1, 1], k=1)[0]
    return tag_len, mki_len


def _pad_to_word(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Ensure total length multiple of 4 bytes
    rem = len(b) & 3
    if rem == 0:
        return b
    return b + b"\x00" * (4 - rem)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Build RTP header
    header = _build_rtp_header(r)

    # Decide SRTP trailer sizes now, to bound payload accordingly
    tag_len, mki_len = _choose_trailer_sizes(r)

    # Compute maximum payload that keeps total <= MAX_TOTAL and still multiple of 4 after padding
    # We'll add: payload + tag_len + mki_len, then pad to 4
    max_payload = MAX_TOTAL - len(header) - tag_len - mki_len
    if max_payload < 0:
        max_payload = 0

    payload = _build_rtp_payload(r, max_payload)

    # Construct SRTP trailer: ciphertext-auth tag (opaque random) + optional MKI
    auth_tag = r.randbytes(tag_len)
    mki = r.randbytes(mki_len) if mki_len else b""

    pkt = header + payload + auth_tag + mki
    pkt = _pad_to_word(pkt)

    # As an additional variation, occasionally add RTP padding bytes (set P bit and pad count)
    # RTP padding adds N pad bytes at end where last byte is pad count. This is before SRTP trailer in real RTP,
    # but since SRTP protects the entire RTP packet then appends trailer, padding would be part of RTP payload.
    # Our earlier payload already covers structure; to avoid conflicting with constructed trailer, we skip here.

    # Ensure non-empty and within limit
    if not pkt:
        pkt = b"\x80\x60\x00\x01" + b"\x00\x00\x00\x00" + b"\x00\x00\x00\x00" + b"\x00" * 12
        pkt = _pad_to_word(pkt)

    # Final safety clamp
    if len(pkt) > MAX_TOTAL:
        pkt = pkt[:MAX_TOTAL & ~3]  # trim to multiple of 4

    return pkt

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator creates valid RTCP packets (byte-aligned to 32-bit, length >= 8)
# matching the fuzzer stub expectations. It builds a variety of RTCP packet types
# and compound packets to exercise srtp_protect_rtcp.

# RTCP packet format (RFC 3550):
# Common header (4 bytes):
#   V=2 (2b), P (1b), RC (5b), PT (8b), length (16b)
# Followed by payload whose size is (length+1)*4 - 4 bytes.
# Total packet size in bytes = (length + 1) * 4.

PT_SR = 200
PT_RR = 201
PT_SDES = 202
PT_BYE = 203
PT_APP = 204
PT_RTPFB = 205
PT_PSFB = 206
PT_XR = 207

SDES_END = 0
SDES_CNAME = 1
SDES_NAME = 2
SDES_EMAIL = 3
SDES_TOOL = 6

MAX_PACKET = 4096


def _pad4(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    pad = (-len(b)) & 3
    if pad:
        b += b"\x00" * pad
    return b


def _rtcp_header(pt: int, rc: int, payload_len_bytes: int, p: int = 0, v: int = 2) -> bytes:
    # length field counts 32-bit words minus one, of the whole packet
    total_len = 4 + payload_len_bytes
    length_words_minus1 = (total_len // 4) - 1
    v_p_rc = (v & 0x3) << 6 | ((p & 0x1) << 5) | (rc & 0x1F)
    return struct.pack('!BBH', v_p_rc, pt & 0xFF, length_words_minus1)


def _sr_block(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Sender Report: SSRC + NTP ts (64) + RTP ts (32) + packet count (32) + octet count (32)
    ssrc = rng.getrandbits(32)
    ntp_sec = rng.getrandbits(32)
    ntp_frac = rng.getrandbits(32)
    rtp_ts = rng.getrandbits(32)
    pkt_cnt = rng.getrandbits(32)
    oct_cnt = rng.getrandbits(32)
    return struct.pack('!LLLLLL', ssrc, ntp_sec, ntp_frac, rtp_ts, pkt_cnt, oct_cnt)


def _rb_block(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Reception report block (24 bytes)
    ssrc = rng.getrandbits(32)
    frac_lost = rng.randrange(0, 256)
    cum_lost = rng.randrange(0, 1 << 24)
    ext_seq = rng.getrandbits(32)
    jitter = rng.getrandbits(32)
    lsr = rng.getrandbits(32)
    dlsr = rng.getrandbits(32)
    return struct.pack('!L', ssrc) + struct.pack('!B', frac_lost) + cum_lost.to_bytes(3, 'big') + \
           struct.pack('!LLLL', ext_seq, jitter, lsr, dlsr)


def _rr_packet(rng: random.Random, rc: int = None) -> bytes:
    if rc is None:
        rc = rng.randrange(0, 5)
    ssrc_sender = rng.getrandbits(32)
    payload = struct.pack('!L', ssrc_sender)
    for _ in range(rc):
        payload += _rb_block(rng)
    hdr = _rtcp_header(PT_RR, rc, len(payload))
    return hdr + payload


def _sr_packet(rng: random.Random, rc: int = None) -> bytes:
    if rc is None:
        rc = rng.randrange(0, 5)
    payload = _sr_block(rng)
    for _ in range(rc):
        payload += _rb_block(rng)
    hdr = _rtcp_header(PT_SR, rc, len(payload))
    return hdr + payload


def _sdes_chunk(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    ssrc = rng.getrandbits(32)
    items = b''
    # Include 1-3 SDES items
    item_types = [SDES_CNAME, SDES_NAME, SDES_TOOL, SDES_EMAIL]
    rng.shuffle(item_types)
    count = rng.randrange(1, 4)
    for t in item_types[:count]:
        # Reasonable ASCII payloads
        choices = {
            SDES_CNAME: [b"user@example.com", b"alice@host", b"cname-123"],
            SDES_NAME: [b"Alice", b"Bob", b"Carol"],
            SDES_TOOL: [b"libwebrtc", b"gstreamer", b"ffmpeg"],
            SDES_EMAIL: [b"dev@example.org", b"ops@example.net"],
        }
        val = rng.choice(choices.get(t, [b"x"]))
        # Clip length to 255 per spec
        val = val[:255]
        items += struct.pack('!BB', t, len(val)) + val
    items += struct.pack('!B', SDES_END)
    items = _pad4(items)
    return struct.pack('!L', ssrc) + items


def _sdes_packet(rng: random.Random, rc: int = None) -> bytes:
    if rc is None:
        rc = rng.randrange(1, 4)
    payload = b''.join(_sdes_chunk(rng) for _ in range(rc))
    hdr = _rtcp_header(PT_SDES, rc, len(payload))
    return hdr + payload


def _bye_packet(rng: random.Random, rc: int = None, with_reason: bool = None) -> bytes:
    if rc is None:
        rc = rng.randrange(1, 4)
    if with_reason is None:
        with_reason = rng.choice([False, True])
    ssrcs = [rng.getrandbits(32) for _ in range(rc)]
    payload = b''.join(struct.pack('!L', s) for s in ssrcs)
    if with_reason:
        reasons = [b"session end", b"test", b"timeout", b"switch"]
        reason = rng.choice(reasons)
        reason = reason[:255]
        payload += struct.pack('!B', len(reason)) + reason
        payload = _pad4(payload)
    hdr = _rtcp_header(PT_BYE, rc, len(payload))
    return hdr + payload


def _app_packet(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    rc = 0
    ssrc = rng.getrandbits(32)
    name = rng.choice([b"TEST", b"APPL", b"DEMO"])  # 4 ASCII
    subtype = rng.randrange(0, 32)
    # Include some arbitrary application data (multiple of 4 bytes)
    data_words = rng.randrange(0, 6)
    app_data = os.urandom(data_words * 4)
    payload = struct.pack('!L', ssrc) + name + app_data
    hdr = _rtcp_header(PT_APP, subtype, len(payload))
    return hdr + payload


def _xr_packet(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal XR with a single empty report block header
    rc = 0
    ssrc = rng.getrandbits(32)
    # One empty block: BT (8), reserved (8), length (16) words excluding this header
    bt = rng.randrange(0, 256)
    block_body = b''
    block_len_words = len(block_body) // 4
    block = struct.pack('!BBH', bt, 0, block_len_words) + block_body
    payload = struct.pack('!L', ssrc) + block
    payload = _pad4(payload)
    hdr = _rtcp_header(PT_XR, rc, len(payload))
    return hdr + payload


def _compound(rng: random.Random, max_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    # Compound RTCP typically starts with SR or RR, then others.
    builders = [_sr_packet, _rr_packet]
    pkt = rng.choice(builders)(rng)
    while True:
        add = rng.choice([_sdes_packet, _bye_packet, _app_packet, _xr_packet])(rng)
        if len(pkt) + len(add) > max_bytes:
            break
        pkt += add
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            break
    return pkt


def _pick_packet(rng: random.Random, budget: int) -> bytes:
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.2:
        return _sr_packet(rng)
    elif choice < 0.4:
        return _rr_packet(rng)
    elif choice < 0.6:
        return _sdes_packet(rng)
    elif choice < 0.75:
        return _bye_packet(rng)
    elif choice < 0.9:
        return _app_packet(rng)
    elif choice < 0.95:
        return _xr_packet(rng)
    else:
        return _compound(rng, budget)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Aim for 8..~1500 bytes, 32-bit aligned, but ensure <= 4096
    budget = min(4096, rng.randrange(8, 1600))
    pkt = _pick_packet(rng, budget)
    # Ensure at least 8 bytes and multiple of 4 (constructors already do so)
    if len(pkt) < 8 or (len(pkt) % 4) != 0:
        pkt = _rr_packet(rng)
    # Truncate if necessary to respect budget (should already fit)
    if len(pkt) > budget:
        # fallback to a minimal RR
        pkt = _rr_packet(rng)
    return pkt[:4096]

import random
import struct
import os

# Generate a minimal but valid-looking RTCP packet and then append an SRTCP trailer
# compatible with libSRTP expectations. While we cannot encrypt/authenticate without
# the session keys, we craft shapes that match SRTCP format so the target will at
# least parse lengths and structure. The fuzzer harness will provide a valid ctx.
#
# SRTCP format (RFC 3711):
# - RTCP packet (common header 4 bytes + payload), 32-bit aligned
# - SRTCP trailer:
#     * 32-bit SRTCP index field: (E bit in MSB) | (31-bit SRTCP index)
#     * If E=1: authentication tag (e.g., 10 or 16 bytes depending on policy)
#     * Optional MKI if policy.use_mki set (we can include or omit; shape remains valid)
#
# We generate various RTCP packet types (SR=200, RR=201, SDES=202, BYE=203, APP=204, XR=207)
# with correct internal length fields so that parsers handling multiple RTCP blocks/compound
# packets get exercised. We also vary the trailer: E bit set/clear, tag length 0/10/16,
# optional MKI of 0/1/4/8 bytes. Total length is kept multiple of 4 and <= 4096.

RTCP_PT_SR = 200
RTCP_PT_RR = 201
RTCP_PT_SDES = 202
RTCP_PT_BYE = 203
RTCP_PT_APP = 204
RTCP_PT_XR = 207

MAX_TOTAL = 4096


def _rtcp_header(rc, pt, length_words, version=2, p=0):
    # RC in lower 5 bits of first byte, P in bit5, V in bits6-7
    v_p_rc = ((version & 0x3) << 6) | ((p & 0x1) << 5) | (rc & 0x1F)
    return struct.pack('!BBH', v_p_rc, pt & 0xFF, length_words & 0xFFFF)


def _pad4(b):
    pad = (-len(b)) & 3
    if pad:
        b += b"\x00" * pad
    return b


def _rtcp_sr():
    # Sender Report: RC = report count (0-31)
    rc = 0
    ssrc = random.getrandbits(32)
    # sender info: NTP timestamp (64), RTP timestamp (32), packet count(32), octet count(32)
    sender_info = struct.pack('!IIIIII',
                              random.getrandbits(32), random.getrandbits(32),
                              random.getrandbits(32), random.getrandbits(32),
                              random.getrandbits(32), random.getrandbits(32))
    report_blocks = b''
    # optionally include 1 report block to exercise parsing
    if random.random() < 0.5:
        rc = 1
        report_blocks += struct.pack('!I', random.getrandbits(32))  # ssrc_n
        report_blocks += struct.pack('!BBBBBBH',
                                     random.getrandbits(8), random.getrandbits(8),
                                     random.getrandbits(8), random.getrandbits(8),
                                     random.getrandbits(8), random.getrandbits(8),
                                     random.getrandbits(16))
        report_blocks += struct.pack('!I', random.getrandbits(32))  # delay since last SR
    body = struct.pack('!I', ssrc) + sender_info + report_blocks
    body = _pad4(body)
    length_words = (len(body) // 4) + 1  # header not counted; length is in 32-bit words minus 1
    return _rtcp_header(rc, RTCP_PT_SR, length_words) + body


def _rtcp_rr():
    rc = 0
    ssrc = random.getrandbits(32)
    blocks = b''
    if random.random() < 0.7:
        rc = random.choice([1, 2])
        for _ in range(rc):
            blocks += struct.pack('!I', random.getrandbits(32))
            blocks += struct.pack('!BBBBBBH',
                                   random.getrandbits(8), random.getrandbits(8),
                                   random.getrandbits(8), random.getrandbits(8),
                                   random.getrandbits(8), random.getrandbits(8),
                                   random.getrandbits(16))
            blocks += struct.pack('!I', random.getrandbits(32))
    body = struct.pack('!I', ssrc) + blocks
    body = _pad4(body)
    length_words = (len(body) // 4) + 1
    return _rtcp_header(rc, RTCP_PT_RR, length_words) + body


def _rtcp_sdes():
    # SDES with one chunk and a CNAME item
    rc = 1
    ssrc = random.getrandbits(32)
    cname = f"user{random.randint(1,9999)}@example.com".encode('ascii')
    item = struct.pack('!BB', 1, len(cname)) + cname  # type 1=CNAME
    # Optionally add another item (TOOL=6 or NOTE=7)
    if random.random() < 0.5:
        tool = b"fuzzer"
        item += struct.pack('!BB', 6, len(tool)) + tool
    item += b"\x00"  # end item type=0
    chunk = struct.pack('!I', ssrc) + item
    chunk = _pad4(chunk)
    body = chunk
    length_words = (len(body) // 4) + 1
    return _rtcp_header(rc, RTCP_PT_SDES, length_words) + body


def _rtcp_bye():
    # BYE with 1 source and optional reason
    rc = 1
    ssrc = random.getrandbits(32)
    body = struct.pack('!I', ssrc)
    if random.random() < 0.5:
        reason = random.choice([b"done", b"test", b"leaving"])[:255]
        body += struct.pack('!B', len(reason)) + reason
    body = _pad4(body)
    length_words = (len(body) // 4) + 1
    return _rtcp_header(rc, RTCP_PT_BYE, length_words) + body


def _rtcp_app():
    # APP packet with name and data
    rc = random.randint(0, 1)
    ssrc = random.getrandbits(32)
    name = random.choice([b"TEST", b"FUZR", b"APPL"])  # 4 ASCII
    data_len = random.choice([0, 4, 8, 12])
    app_data = os.urandom(data_len)
    body = struct.pack('!I4s', ssrc, name) + app_data
    body = _pad4(body)
    length_words = (len(body) // 4) + 1
    return _rtcp_header(rc, RTCP_PT_APP, length_words) + body


def _rtcp_xr():
    # Minimal XR with one empty report block header (type + len)
    rc = 0
    ssrc = random.getrandbits(32)
    # Report block header: BT(8), reserved(8), block length (16) in 32-bit words minus 1
    block = struct.pack('!BBH', 0, 0, 0)  # zero-length block
    body = struct.pack('!I', ssrc) + block
    body = _pad4(body)
    length_words = (len(body) // 4) + 1
    return _rtcp_header(rc, RTCP_PT_XR, length_words) + body


def _build_compound_rtcp(max_len):
    # Build 1-3 RTCP packets forming a compound packet
    builders = [_rtcp_sr, _rtcp_rr, _rtcp_sdes, _rtcp_bye, _rtcp_app, _rtcp_xr]
    random.shuffle(builders)
    count = random.randint(1, 3)
    pkt = b''
    for i in range(count):
        b = builders[i % len(builders)]()
        if len(pkt) + len(b) > max_len:
            break
        pkt += b
    return pkt


def _srtcp_trailer():
    # Choose E bit and index; choose tag length consistent with common profiles
    e_bit = 1 if random.random() < 0.8 else 0
    index = random.getrandbits(31) & 0x7FFFFFFF
    srtcp_index = ((e_bit & 1) << 31) | index
    trailer = struct.pack('!I', srtcp_index)

    # Tag length: typical HMAC-SHA1 80 -> 10 bytes, or GCM 16 -> 16 bytes
    tag_len = 0
    if e_bit == 1:
        tag_len = random.choice([10, 16])
        trailer += os.urandom(tag_len)

    # Optional MKI (0/1/4/8 bytes)
    if random.random() < 0.3:
        mki_len = random.choice([1, 4, 8])
        trailer += os.urandom(mki_len)

    trailer = _pad4(trailer)
    return trailer


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    random.seed(seed)
    # Reserve space for a reasonably sized SRTCP packet
    # We target between 64 and 1500 bytes typically, but cap at MAX_TOTAL
    target = random.randint(64, min(1500, MAX_TOTAL))

    # Build RTCP part first
    # Ensure we leave space for trailer (up to ~32 bytes)
    max_rtcp = max(8, target - 64)
    rtcp = _build_compound_rtcp(max_rtcp)
    if len(rtcp) < 8:
        # Fallback to a single RR if somehow empty
        rtcp = _rtcp_rr()

    trailer = _srtcp_trailer()
    pkt = rtcp + trailer

    # Ensure total length is a multiple of 4 and at least 8 bytes (fuzzer also enforces)
    pkt = _pad4(pkt)
    if len(pkt) > MAX_TOTAL:
        pkt = pkt[:MAX_TOTAL - (MAX_TOTAL % 4)]
        pkt = _pad4(pkt)

    return pkt

import random
from typing import Tuple

# Generator for: SRTP master key+salt concatenation
# Target fuzz stubs query a profile, then call:
#   klen = srtp_profile_get_master_key_length(profile)
#   slen = srtp_profile_get_master_salt_length(profile)
# and expect FUZZ_PARAM_STR to contain at least klen+slen bytes that will be copied
# directly (raw) as key||salt. Our generate() returns such concatenations.
#
# Profiles and typical lengths in libSRTP (bytes):
# - srtp_profile_aes128_cm_sha1_*: key=16, salt=14
# - srtp_profile_null_sha1_*:      key=0 (but lib typically still expects material when policy set
#                                  via profile setters used by the fuzzer). To remain valid for
#                                  all stubs that enforce klen>0 and slen>0, we avoid profiles
#                                  with zero lengths and provide sets with positive lengths.
# - srtp_profile_aead_aes_128_gcm: key=16, salt=12
# - srtp_profile_aead_aes_256_gcm: key=32, salt=12
# Some builds may vary, so we provide multiple candidate sizes and pick one seeded-randomly.

# Candidate (key_len, salt_len) tuples kept <= 2048 total
CANDIDATE_SIZES: Tuple[Tuple[int, int], ...] = (
    (16, 14),   # AES-128 CM + HMAC-SHA1 (common)
    (16, 12),   # AEAD AES-128-GCM
    (32, 14),   # AES-256 CM + HMAC-SHA1 (some profiles)
    (32, 12),   # AEAD AES-256-GCM
    (24, 14),   # AES-192 CM + HMAC-SHA1 (supported by some builds)
    (24, 12),   # hypothetical AEAD-192 (kept as variety; still valid raw material)
)

# Byte patterns that are often interesting for crypto code paths but remain valid:
# - all-zero key/salt
# - all-0xFF
# - incrementing bytes
# - random bytes
# - structured: key=zero, salt=random; key=random, salt=zero
# The fuzzer stubs do not validate contents, only sizes, so these are valid.

def _pattern_all(b: int, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([b]) * n


def _pattern_inc(n: int, start: int = 0) -> bytes:
    return bytes((start + i) & 0xFF for i in range(n))


def _pattern_random(n: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return rng.randbytes(n)


def _mix(a: bytes, b: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Simple interleave half/half to create variability while staying valid bytes
    mid = min(len(a), len(b)) // 2
    return a[:mid] + b[:mid] + a[mid:] + b[mid:]


def _build_material(klen: int, slen: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose among several deterministic patterns based on rng state
    choice = rng.randrange(0, 8)
    if choice == 0:
        key = _pattern_all(0x00, klen)
        salt = _pattern_all(0x00, slen)
    elif choice == 1:
        key = _pattern_all(0xFF, klen)
        salt = _pattern_all(0xFF, slen)
    elif choice == 2:
        key = _pattern_inc(klen, start=rng.randrange(0, 256))
        salt = _pattern_inc(slen, start=rng.randrange(0, 256))
    elif choice == 3:
        key = _pattern_random(klen, rng)
        salt = _pattern_random(slen, rng)
    elif choice == 4:
        key = _pattern_all(0x00, klen)
        salt = _pattern_random(slen, rng)
    elif choice == 5:
        key = _pattern_random(klen, rng)
        salt = _pattern_all(0x00, slen)
    elif choice == 6:
        key = _pattern_inc(klen, start=0)
        salt = _pattern_all(0xAA, slen)
    else:
        # blend deterministic and random
        key = _mix(_pattern_inc(klen, start=1), _pattern_random(klen, rng))[:klen]
        salt = _mix(_pattern_inc(slen, start=2), _pattern_random(slen, rng))[:slen]
    return key + salt


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Pick a candidate size. Favor common GCM/CM sizes but vary deterministically.
    # Weight common ones slightly higher.
    weights = [4, 4, 2, 3, 1, 1]
    cum = []
    s = 0
    for w in weights:
        s += w
        cum.append(s)
    r = rng.randrange(s)
    idx = 0
    for i, c in enumerate(cum):
        if r < c:
            idx = i
            break
    klen, slen = CANDIDATE_SIZES[idx]

    # Build valid key||salt buffer
    material = _build_material(klen, slen, rng)

    # Ensure upper bound (<= 4096) as required
    if len(material) > 4096:
        material = material[:4096]

    return material

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets FUZZ_PARAM_STR used as a debug module name for
# srtp_set_debug_module(mod_name, on). The library expects recognizable module
# names. We provide a pool of plausible names seen in libSRTP plus variations,
# and also generate random-but-valid UTF-8 strings to explore paths where the
# module is unknown (should return error or success depending on build).
# The fuzzer stub bails if return status is not ok, so we bias toward likely
# valid names to keep inputs interesting and accepted.

KNOWN_MODULES = [
    # Common libSRTP debug modules (typical names across versions/builds)
    "srtp",
    "rtp",
    "rtcp",
    "auth",
    "cipher",
    "crypto",
    "policy",
    "rdbx",
    "replay",
    "alloc",
    "err",
    "aes",
    "aes_gcm",
    "hmac",
    "kernel",
    "null",
    # Variants with case/formatting sometimes seen
    "SRTP",
    "RTP",
    "RTCP",
    "AUTH",
    "CIPHER",
    "CRYPTO",
    "POLICY",
    "RDBX",
    "REPLAY",
    "ALLOC",
    "ERR",
    "AES",
    "AES_GCM",
    "HMAC",
]

UNICODE_WORDS = [
    "модуль",
    "模块",
    "モジュール",
    "모듈",
    "מודול",
    "unidad",
    "modulo",
    "module",
    "módulo",
]

ASCII_EXTRA = "-_:./+@#"


def _rand_choice_weighted(r: random.Random, items: List[str], weights: List[float]) -> str:
    # simple weighted choice without numpy
    total = sum(weights)
    x = r.random() * total
    acc = 0.0
    for item, w in zip(items, weights):
        acc += w
        if x <= acc:
            return item
    return items[-1]


def _random_utf8(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Generate valid UTF-8 string comprised of ASCII + selected non-ASCII words
    # to remain human-readable while exploring UTF-8 handling.
    parts: List[str] = []
    length = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    while len("".join(parts)) < length:
        choice = r.randint(0, 9)
        if choice < 6:
            parts.append(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + ASCII_EXTRA))
        elif choice < 8:
            parts.append(r.choice([" ", "-", "_", "."]))
        else:
            parts.append(r.choice(UNICODE_WORDS))
    s = "".join(parts)
    # Trim to requested length range conservatively
    if len(s) > max_len:
        s = s[:max_len]
    if len(s) < min_len:
        s = (s + "x" * min_len)[:min_len]
    return s


def _make_module_candidate(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Strategy mix: known good names, known variants, namespaced, prefixed/suffixed,
    # and random UTF-8 tokens that still look like module names.
    strategies = [
        "known",
        "known_case_variant",
        "namespaced",
        "pref_suf",
        "random_utf8_short",
        "random_utf8_long",
    ]
    weights = [0.45, 0.1, 0.15, 0.1, 0.15, 0.05]
    strat = _rand_choice_weighted(r, strategies, weights)

    if strat == "known":
        return r.choice(KNOWN_MODULES)

    if strat == "known_case_variant":
        base = r.choice(KNOWN_MODULES)
        variant = r.choice([str.upper, str.lower, str.title])
        return variant(base)

    if strat == "namespaced":
        ns = r.choice(["srtp", "org.srtp", "net.srtp", "lib.srtp", "webrtc", "app"]) \
             + r.choice([".", ":", "/", "_"])
        mod = r.choice(KNOWN_MODULES)
        extra = ""
        if r.random() < 0.4:
            extra = r.choice([".detail", ".debug", ".test", ".perf"]) \
                    + ("." + r.choice(["v1", "v2", "stable", "exp"]) if r.random() < 0.5 else "")
        return ns + mod + extra

    if strat == "pref_suf":
        base = r.choice(KNOWN_MODULES)
        pre = r.choice(["", "dbg_", "mod_", "lib_", "sr_", ""]) \
              + ("" if r.random() < 0.6 else r.choice(["aes_", "rtp_", "rtcp_"]))
        suf = r.choice(["", "_debug", "_trace", "_test", "_perf"]) \
              + ("" if r.random() < 0.7 else r.choice(["_v1", "_v2"]))
        return pre + base + suf

    if strat == "random_utf8_short":
        return _random_utf8(r, 3, 16)

    if strat == "random_utf8_long":
        return _random_utf8(r, 8, 48)

    return r.choice(KNOWN_MODULES)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Sometimes produce multiple candidates concatenated with NULs so the fuzz
    # harness can pick various substrings if it scans or splits; but keep within
    # a single valid C-string by ending at first NUL. For FUZZ_PARAM_STR, the
    # harness typically uses the entire buffer as a C++ std::string, so avoid NULs.
    # We therefore avoid embedding NULs to keep the module name intact.

    # Bias toward names likely to exist to avoid early bailouts in the stub.
    s = _make_module_candidate(r)

    # Ensure non-empty and length limit
    if not s:
        s = "srtp"
    s = s[:256]

    # Return UTF-8 bytes
    return s.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")
